title: Unsafe-reuse audit: repeated cache keys and the effect filter they require

question_map.d: first_trial.b and first_trial.c (the two counts restricted to first-trial records)

effect_map.scope: covers the 26 tau-bench tools only: class, entity, entity_keys, for examples/real_traces/tau_bench_historical.jsonl
effect_map.how_used: imported at build time and authoritative for every tau-bench tool: its class decides b/c and its entity/entity_keys decide which id is compared. Its vocabulary is read/write/control, mapped to this audit's read/write/other (control -> other)
effect_map.not_covered_there: swe-agent bash verbs and the agentgym action set are outside that map; they are derived here and flagged per tool in derived_effect_classes.tool_table.class_source
effect_map.timing: absent when this audit started and created by task A1 while it ran; the sha256 above pins the exact version whose classes these numbers were computed from, and rebuilding against an edited map is expected to move them
effect_map.created_nothing: this audit wrote no file at that path

excluded.reason: workflow definition (steps + declared side_effects); no tool-call records, so no (tool,args) key exists to repeat
same: workflow definition, no tool-call records

definitions.record: one line of a corpus file = one task attempt (one trajectory)
definitions.key: sha256(tool || canonical-json(arguments)); the key a (tool,args) cache uses
definitions.repeat: a key with two or more occurrences
definitions.run: one corpus file x one source label = one evaluation campaign. The two tau-bench files reuse the same source labels for disjoint task splits, so a file is part of the run identity; merging them is measured in sensitivity.run_equals_source
definitions.task_uid: domain::task_id (the model is not part of task identity)
definitions.within_task: all occurrences of the key fall in one record; it repeats nowhere else
definitions.within_run_across_tasks: the key occurs in two or more records inside one run, but in only one run
definitions.cross_run: the key occurs in two or more runs
definitions.scope_rule: the three buckets are exclusive and assigned by widest span (cross_run > within_run_across_tasks > within_task); a.repeated_keys_by_scope sums to a.repeated_keys while a.nested_repeat_levels counts the levels non-exclusively
definitions.first_trial: records with trial in (None, 0), the pilot's headline convention
definitions.stale_read: a read key that repeats inside one scope and whose entity was written by an earlier call in that scope, so the cached answer predates the write

effect_classes.write: mutates entity state; a hit serves the call without performing it
effect_classes.other: side-effect-free on the store but not an entity read: navigation, scroll, think/calculate, submit

class_derivation.tau-bench tools: examples/benchmarks/tool_effect_map.json (task A1's map: 26 tools, class + entity + entity_keys, imported at build time)
class_derivation.swe-agent bash: per-invocation verb table; verbs outside the table are writes (conservative)
class_derivation.agentgym: derived here: navigation -> other, look/inventory/examine/select -> read, manipulation -> write

entity_rules.tau-bench: tool_effect_map.json entity + entity_keys; a handle is (entity, value of that argument key), so order#W1 read and order#W1 written compare equal while user#email never equals user#user_id
entity_rules.swe-agent: the file path token of the command; edits and file reads on the same path share an entity
entity_rules.agentgym: examine -> object name; open/close -> receptacle; put -> object + receptacle
entity_rules.no_entity: name lookups, list_*, flight search, navigation, think/calculate, sqlgym table sets are entity-bearing only for select (tables)

reproduce.determinism: same inputs -> identical bytes; no timestamps, no eval order, sorted dicts
reproduce.inputs_pinned: corpus sha256 per file in provenance.corpus, effect map sha256 in provenance.effect_map; if a file's digest moves, every count here is stale
reproduce.algorithm: for each call build key=sha256(tool|sorted args), classify the effect, extract entity handles; group occurrences by key; assign a repeat to within_task / within_run_across_tasks / cross_run by widest span; count write-class repeats (b); for (c) walk each run and each task attempt in recorded order, let the first occurrence of a read key populate the cache and flag a later occurrence when a write to the same entity handle lands between them

known_limitations: sqlgym select arguments carry only the table set, not the SQL text, so its keys are degenerate; its repeats are real key repeats but the trace cannot show whether the queries were equal
agentgym entity names are receptacle/object classes (e.g. cabinet), not instances; cross-task entity identity in an embodied benchmark is a class match, not an object match
the four corpora reset environment state per task attempt, so run-scope staleness (c.scope_run) holds only under a shared-store assumption; c.scope_task does not need it
no timing information is retained, so 'earlier' means earlier in recorded call order
the corpus is an inputs-only capture; it never shows what a tool returned, so staleness is inferred from the write/read order, not observed

bash_as_monolithic_write.why: the pilot's convention treats every bash call as effectful; this shows what (b)/(c) become without the verb refinement

run_equals_source.why: merges the two tau-bench capture files under one source label; shows how much of cross_run is a run-identity artifact

unknown_bash_verbs_as_read.why: lower bound on write repeats: verbs outside the table are reads instead of writes

paper_claim.load_bearing: all_trials.b.repeated_write_keys (and first_trial.b for the headline sample)
paper_claim.why: it needs no assumption about entity identity or state sharing: a cache keyed on (tool,args) that stores writes replays them, and the replay is what the caller asked to happen but which did not happen
paper_claim.supporting: c bounds the second failure mode (a read answered from a pre-write value). c.scope_task is the variant that survives per-task state reset; c.scope_run is the run-scoped upper bound the task asked for

stale.scope: tau-bench only: 4 source runs (gpt-4o-retail, gpt-4o-airline, sonnet-35-new-retail, sonnet-35-new-airline), first trial of each task, file order. Counts *hits* answered from a value that predates a write to the same entity; the corpus-wide key-level companion is first_trial.c / all_trials.c above, which counts read keys, not hits.

provenance.streams: 4 runs, first trial per task (325 records, 2,275 calls), file order
provenance.positions: 0-based call index within a run, every call counted
provenance.cache: one per run, first insertion wins, unbounded residency

reset_reading.assumption: tau-bench runs every task attempt in a fresh environment built from the domain's base data, so a cached value captured before any write of its own task equals the state the hit's task starts from
reset_reading.note: a window inside a failed episode cannot be shown to have served a wrong value, because the write may have been rejected; all five sit in reward-0 episodes, so this corpus exhibits unjustified hits, not an observable wrong replay

counterfactual.description: the same stream with a cache that drops a read's key when its entity is written; the gap to the 746 hits is what coherence costs this run

reconciliation.note: one read key can be answered stale several times, which is why 113 keys carry the 169 hits; these per-run key counts are the tau_bench_historical rows of first_trial.c.scope_run.by_run

all_trials.description: the same audit over every record: trial replay re-runs one conversation against a reset backend, which inflates hits, stale windows and duplicate writes, so this is a bound, not a headline

unjoined.note: reads and writes that share no id are never counted as stale, and product reads cannot be joined to item ids from another namespace, so every count here is a lower bound on staleness

sensitivity.write_success: the corpus records inputs only, so whether a write call landed is not observable; episode_reward splits the windows by the reward of the write's episode and of the hit's episode
